Summary: Judge your neighbour in righteousness: the verdict follows the truth of the cause, not the standing of the parties.
Application: Righteous judgment is the positive side of impartiality — not merely refusing bribes and favour, but actively weighing the cause aright. A righteous verdict is the aim; impartiality is the guardrail that gets the judge there.
Purpose: TRADITIONAL reading: righteous judgment weighs the cause itself, with neither fear nor favour toward the parties.
